_comment: The schema of the okf_check: block in okf-base.yaml. okf-verify enforces it (okf-verify --check-config) and okf-check calls that, so the two tools cannot disagree. A node is {keys: {name: node}} (a mapping with exactly those keys), {map: node} (a mapping with free non-empty string keys, each value a node), {list: node} (a list whose items are node), {enum: [values]} (one of those strings), {type: boolean} (true or false) or {type: string} (a non-empty string). A node under keys may add {requires: {sibling: value}}: the key is only valid when that sibling has that value. A map node may add {key_no_prefix: !}: no key may start with that text. To add an option, add its key under the top-level keys.
